name: Orthogonality and Least Squares
description: Project onto a subspace and fit the best line when no exact answer exists.

lessonNames.l9-line-misses: When the line misses the points
lessonNames.l11-fitting-a-line: Fitting a line by least squares
lessonNames.l12-beta-by-hand: A stock’s beta by least squares

lessonObjectives.l1-perpendicular: Test vectors and subspaces for orthogonality.
lessonObjectives.l2-four-subspaces: Show that the nullspace is perpendicular to the row space.
lessonObjectives.l3-orthonormal: Use orthonormal bases and orthogonal matrices to simplify calculations.
lessonObjectives.l4-straightening: Apply Gram-Schmidt to build an orthonormal basis.
lessonObjectives.l5-dropping-a-perpendicular: Project a vector onto a line.
lessonObjectives.l6-projection-matrix: Build the matrix that projects onto a column space.
lessonObjectives.l7-error-perpendicular: Show that the projection error is orthogonal to the space.
lessonObjectives.l8-qr: Factor $A = QR$ and see why it makes least squares stable.
lessonObjectives.l9-line-misses: See why an overdetermined system has no exact solution.
lessonObjectives.l10-normal-equations: Derive $A^T A \hat{\mathbf{x}} = A^T \mathbf{b}$ from the projection.
lessonObjectives.l11-fitting-a-line: Fit a line to data with the normal equations.
lessonObjectives.l12-beta-by-hand: Estimate a stock’s beta in NumPy from matrix operations alone.
